title: A short history of the honey trap
gist: Former CIA officer Marc Polymeropoulos, prompted by a current tabloid spy scandal, surveys honey-trap espionage from Mata Hari to Stasi 'Romeos' and KGB cases, framed by the MICE recruitment model. He argues US intelligence avoids honey traps for practical reasons: blackmailed agents are less productive and reliable than those motivated by ideology or money, and the tactic barely works on cultures, like France, where affairs carry little stigma.

themes.theme: MICE recruitment model and the honey trap

insights.claim: Marc Polymeropoulos explains that intelligence services recruit targets using the 'MICE' principle—Money, Ideology, Coercion and Ego—exploiting a target's vulnerabilities, with honey traps falling under coercion.
insights.speaker: Marc Polymeropoulos
insights.so_what: A useful lens for assessing insider-threat and espionage risk to firms and governments holding sensitive information.
insights.quote: An intelligence service seeks to recruit targets based on the ‘MICE’ principle, which includes Money, Ideology, Coercion and Ego as key motivating factors.

insights.claim: Polymeropoulos argues that, per open-source reporting, US intelligence avoids honey traps not out of squeamishness but because blackmailed agents are less productive, trustworthy and durable than agents motivated by ideology, such as hatred of communism, or money.
insights.speaker: Marc Polymeropoulos
insights.so_what: Coercion-based leverage yields poor long-term returns versus aligned incentives, a lesson applicable beyond espionage.
insights.quote: Blackmail doesn’t make for productive long-term agents, many former case officers say.

insights.claim: Honey traps do not work on all targets because culture matters: a French intelligence officer notes that extramarital affairs are so commonplace in France that threatening exposure gives a hostile service little leverage.
insights.speaker: Marc Polymeropoulos
insights.so_what: Coercive leverage depends on social stigma; vulnerability profiles vary by culture.

insights.so_what: Honey traps target staff with access, not just principals, so secretaries and support personnel are a key insider-risk vector.
